narrative.overview: Fin-Agent looks like a first-party system app, not a finance dashboard. The ground is true black, surfaces are graphite, and the only saturated colours are the ones that mean something: blue for action, green for a floor that holds, amber for money that is due, red for money that is not there. Type is the platform's own face, so the interface feels installed rather than visited. The product's distinctive surface is the computed receipt: a verdict, the probability that the floor holds against its threshold, the lowest median with its date, the reason, the source count, and one disclosure that opens the curve, tradeoffs, and the rows behind it.
keyCharacteristics: True-black ground; graphite surfaces; 1px hairline borders instead of shadows.
System type (SF on Apple, Segoe on Windows) with tabular numerals.
One action blue; semantic green, amber, red only where money state changes.
The receipt is the signature component; the chat is the shell.
Flat at rest; depth appears only on the composer and the phone sheet.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue is reserved for actions and the user's own voice. If a screen has two blues competing for attention, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Meaning Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red may only appear where they carry a money state.

rules.name: The 68ch Rule
rules.body: Assistant prose never exceeds 68 characters per line, even when the card beside it is wider.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: If a boundary needs to be visible, use a 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.10) line, not a shadow. Shadows lift; borders separate.

dos: Do keep the ground true black and put every surface on Graphite with a 1px hairline.
Do set every amount in tabular numerals at the largest size the hierarchy allows.
Do show the verdict, the probability, and the source count before any explanation.
Do keep the composer pinned and the last message visible above it.
Do use the platform's system font; never ship a display face for the interface.
Do pair every warning colour with the number and date that caused it.
donts: Don't nest cards. The assistant's surface is the page; the card is the only raised object.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow above a heading; the heading carries its own weight.
Don't use blue for anything that is not actionable or the user's own voice.
Don't hide a destination behind horizontal scrolling on phone; the Areas sheet exists.
Don't add a gradient, glass, texture, or themed motif that is not data.
Don't state a number in prose without its receipt or its source chip.
Don't let a receipt's detail view become raw JSON as the first layer.
